abstract.text: An event’s version counts the changes that records stored before them can’t be read through, and only those. A compatible change keeps the version; a breaking one raises it.

Records are never migrated from one version to another, and a record is never delivered with a

The tracking plan (
) exports each event’s version, and its check compares the
events with the committed plan: a breaking change at the version the plan has fails it, with a line
naming the event, the property and the change. With the version raised, the check reports only the
raise, and exporting the plan again writes the new version’s document beside the index.

The check treats a few more changes as breaking: a renamed or removed event; a default value
removed from a required property, as a record stored before the property was added can’t be read;
and a tightened constraint (
), which rejects values an earlier release tracked.
A change of meaning alone, such as a property that keeps its name and type but is measured in other
units, raises the version too. Its records would still read, and raising the version keeps them
from being read as the new meaning.

abstract.text: What each module can collect, the required-reason APIs it calls, and the privacy manifest it ships, so you can fill in your app’s own manifest and privacy labels.
Vendor-neutral analytics for Swift: typed events, tracked by a tracker and delivered in batches to any number of destinations.
Four signals, four jobs. Decide which one a fact belongs to before you write the line that records it.
Traffluent knows people only by a pseudonymous session. An identifier that outlives one is yours to add, store, reset and gate with consent.
